chunks: My father and Muḥammad ibn Ya‘qūb and the group of my scholars (may God have mercy on them) narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, who said:

I was in Fayd, so I walked with ‘Alī ibn Bilāl to the grave of Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl ibn Bazī‘. He said to me: ‘Alī ibn Bilāl said to me: The owner of this grave narrated to me from Imam Riḍā (peace be upon him), who said: Whoever visits the grave of his believing brother, then places his hand on the grave, and recites “Innā Anzalnāh” seven times, will be safe on the Day of Great Terror.

key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ: Inna Anzalnahu (Surah Al-Qadr, 'We have sent it down')
key_terms.صَاحِبُ هَذَا الْقَبْرِ: the owner of this grave (the deceased buried there)
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْفَزَعِ الْأَكْبَرِ: the Day of Great Terror (Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting a believer's grave and reciting Surah Inna Anzalnahu?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the intercessory role of the deceased believer, who conveys a specific instruction from Imam al-Rida (AS) regarding the ritual of touching the grave and reciting Surah Al-Qadr seven times. The promise of safety from the 'Great Terror' (Yawm al-Faza' al-Akbar) underscores the eschatological significance of these visits in Shia tradition, linking the tranquility of the grave to the ultimate deliverance on Judgment Day.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. My father, Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb, and all of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, who said:

I was in Fayd with ‘Ali ibn Bilāl and we walked to the grave of Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’. (Once we arrived at his grave), ‘Ali ibn Bilāl said to me: The owner of this grave narrated to me from Imam Riďā (a.s.), who said: Those who go to the graves of their brothers from among the believers, place their hands on the graves, and recite (the chapter of) “Innā Anzalnāh” seven times will be safe on the Day of Great Terror (the Day of Judgment).
